pr.title: Star items and show only the starred ones

acceptance.evidence: migrations/0002_add_starred.sql adds starred NOT NULL DEFAULT 0 with a CHECK. test/starred.test.js 'AC-1' asserts the three seeded items are 0 and that a value of 2 is rejected.
test 'AC-2' stars item 2 and expects exactly ['First item','★ Second item','Third item']. The src/index.js item() renderer matches.
test 'AC-3' stars items 3 and 1 and expects ['★ First item','★ Third item'], so the order is by id. The query uses WHERE starred = 1 ORDER BY id.
test 'AC-4' checks '/' and '/?show=all' return all items in id order. The default show is 'all'.
test 'AC-5' checks the 'Starred only' link on the full list and the 'All items' link on the starred list.
test 'AC-6' checks the values Starred, none, empty and __proto__ each return 400 with no <li>. The Object.hasOwn guard in src/index.js handles __proto__.
traffic/routes.json contains '/?show=starred'. test 'AC-7' asserts it. The traffic-config check was widened to allow a query string and tests/traffic-config.test.sh covers that.

findings.what: The README mentions ?show=starred but not that `show=all` is accepted or that any other `show` value answers 400. A reader of the README alone would not learn that.
findings.fix: Add a short note: `show` is `all` (default) or `starred`; anything else answers 400.

findings.what: AC-7 only checks that routes.json contains the string. It does not check that the traffic worker actually requests the query string. The edit to test/traffic.test.js makes the fake app record the query, but no test asserts that the starred path is requested.
findings.fix: Have the traffic round test assert that the fake app saw '/?show=starred'.

lenses.note: The spec has a go dated 2026-10-12 and both decisions are followed: starred items keep their place, and the view is a query parameter. No acceptance item was edited after the go, and the change adds nothing beyond the spec.
All 7 items are met. All 4 state rows have tests under describe('states').

vitest isn't installed here, so I couldn't run `npm test`. CI (.github/workflows/ci.yml) runs `npm test` and tests/run.sh on every push. The tests assert behaviour. The only edit to an existing test is the traffic fake app, which now records the query string; that is justified by the new route.
README updated. One low gap on the 400 behaviour.
The view lookup uses Object.hasOwn, so prototype keys like __proto__ are rejected. The SQL is built only from the fixed VIEWS table, not from user input. Titles are escaped.

There is no injection path: the query string only selects a key in VIEWS and titles are HTML-escaped. The traffic route regex change still refuses spaces and '#'. I found no instructions planted in the repository.
The diff adds only a plain HTML link and a star character; there are no UI or style files.
The diff touches no UI or style files, so there is no flow to exercise beyond the tests.
The title is 'Star items and show only the starred ones', under 72 characters. The claims match the diff, including the traffic route check change and the fake app change.
